report:
Fresh review of the current claim, both ordinary implementation associations and all eleven ordinary test associations. No TODO/N/A entries exist. The claim requires stash-local interning of values and slices by typed structural content, equal-content handle reuse, and collision resolution by actual equality. The current Stash owns its intern_map; alloc uses TypeId of StaticSelf, element count one, hash, and collision ordinal, checks the candidate's actual T with PartialEq, and reuses only equal candidates. alloc_slice includes length in hashing and key, compares complete typed slices and otherwise advances the collision ordinal. Iterator allocation collects then delegates; append and deep-copy allocation paths delegate to these same operations. push_raw, read_one/read_slice and make_ptr/make_slice retain entry identity and content. Count in the key prevents reading an empty-slice entry as a scalar. Type identity relies on the documented unsafe StashData obligation that distinct types have distinct StaticSelf. InternHasher hashes child content from inline hashes; canonical child handles within this stash supply structural equality to derived parent comparisons. Macro generation hashes named/tuple fields in order and enum discriminants and fields, without padding. Both essential implementation files are already associated; the current extra Stashed::new associations do not alter allocation behavior.
All associated test bodies were inspected. alloc_same_value_deduplicates and hash_cons_distinct assert equal/unequal scalar handles; hash_cons_slice_dedup and hash_cons_slice_distinct assert equal/unequal slice handles. hash_cons_compound_type asserts canonical handles for a derived pair of child pointers. dedup_different_types_same_bits asserts successful typed retrieval of Name and Tag; captured fixtures show their field widths differ, so the additional typed_scalars_slices_and_derived_nested_values_deduplicate test supplies same-width u32/i32 retrieval evidence. That latter test also asserts repeated scalar reuse, iterator/slice equivalence for child pointer slices, derived Branch scalar and slice reuse and empty-slice/empty-iterator equivalence. hash_cons_collision_stores_both supplies a local constant hash implementation and asserts different handles and correct contents for unequal scalar colliders and reversed slices, plus canonical handles for repeated equal content. derived_values_and_slices_resolve_forced_hash_collisions_by_content performs the same checks through derive-generated hashing; captured DerivedCollision and EmptySliceCollision prove the field hash is constant. scalar_collision_with_empty_slice_never_reads_a_slice_as_a_scalar exercises the identical scalar/empty-slice hash in both insertion orders and asserts correct values and canonical handles. empty_unit_slice_and_scalar_do_not_confuse_interning exercises zero-sized values and empty slices. These combined assertions detect accidental sharing on hash equality as well as failure to reuse equal content. Stash-local scope does not promise cross-stash handle identity.
Dependencies captured with review read: arena fixture definitions/imports, Branch and EmptySliceCollision definitions and hash implementation, and DerivedCollision definition. All other implementation helpers used are inside the initial whole-file snapshots. No implementation or test edits are necessary. This refreshed assessment is source inspection; no test suite was executed during this refresh, because the coordinator runs final suites centrally. Earlier execution is not claimed as final-source execution.
